gaps.text: In-line measurement of Medium turbidity / cell density with turbidity/optical-density sensor
In-line measurement of Temperature at the measurement point with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion: Raman and MIR-ATR probes must sample the same small area, ideally via a combined probe, since alternating separate probes cannot guarantee the same spot. Data from the two methods must be synchronised to a common time step and block-scaled before fusion, starting from one model per method. The fused model must beat the best single method on held-out runs, otherwise the second instrument is dropped.)
Achievable fiber link length for this installation: long cables are documented only for silica fibers, and no source states an achievable MIR link length.

items.finding: Low-level data fusion is described as the simplest way to combine inputs, by rearranging variables from different sources into a single data matrix placed one after the other.
items.how_it_applies: This supports the gap's premise that a low-level fusion of Raman and MIR-ATR data is a recognised starting approach; a pilot could begin with one model per method and then test a concatenated matrix. Whether the fused model outperforms the best single method must be verified on held-out runs.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The review describes general methodology, not cell culture spectroscopy, and does not state any performance gain, so no benefit can be assumed for this installation.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E01 ¶31

items.finding: Before fusing data from multiple sources, the contribution of each dataset and its complementarity should be evaluated.
items.how_it_applies: This suggests the pilot should first quantify what each single method (Raman, MIR-ATR) contributes against the laboratory glucose and lactate reference before committing to a fused model, and drop the second instrument if it adds nothing.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement is a general PAT recommendation from a review, not a result from bioprocess media, so the actual complementarity of Raman and MIR-ATR in this medium remains to be tested.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
citation.label: E01 ¶82

items.finding: A cited Raman and FT-IR food study showed that instrument complementarity alone was sometimes not sufficient to improve prediction of several quality attributes.
items.how_it_applies: This is a caution that adding a second spectroscopy method does not automatically improve predictions, so the fused model should be benchmarked against the best single method on held-out runs before keeping both instruments.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The evidence comes from a food analytical study, not cell culture, and involves FT-IR rather than specifically MIR-ATR probe configurations, so the outcome may differ here.

citation.quote: In some situations, instrument complementarity (not data complementarity) was not sufficient to improve the performance of predictive several CQAs, as shown by a Raman and FT-IR data based food analytical study [73].
citation.label: E01 ¶36

items.finding: The OH bands in aqueous solution are temperature sensitive in both NIR and MIR, which the review notes makes tempered sample holders necessary.
items.how_it_applies: This indicates that temperature at the measurement point is relevant to spectral interpretation in aqueous media, so recording temperature alongside the spectra during the pilot would be prudent. It does not establish that a specific temperature sensor is required or sufficient.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The statement concerns sample holders in laboratory NIR/MIR measurement, not an in situ probe in a changing bioreactor, so transfer to an in-line temperature reading is indirect.

citation.quote: Additionally, the temperature sensitivity of the OH bands is a severe drawback for measuring aqueous solution in NIR and MIR, which makes tempered sample holders necessary [29].
citation.label: E02 ¶12

items.finding: When selecting a fiber-optic probe for turbid media, the desired sampling volume where optical scattering is significant is an important selection question.
items.how_it_applies: Since the cell population changes during the run, turbidity-related scattering will vary; the pilot should consider how the chosen probe's sampling volume interacts with changing turbidity when comparing spectra to off-line references.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source discusses probe selection for turbid media generally, not cell density measurement or a specific turbidity sensor, so it does not evidence that in-line turbidity measurement is achievable here.

citation.quote: An important question when selecting a fiber-optic probe for measurements in turbid media or solids is the desired sampling volume where optical scattering is significant.
citation.label: E03 ¶7
